name: rn-predictive-back-brownfield
description: Brownfield demo for Android predictive back, on react-native-brownfield. Native screen -> React Native screen -> native screen with an embedded RN fragment. react-native is symlinked from a local checkout by scripts/link.js; @callstack/react-native-brownfield comes from npm.
//: react-native is replaced by a symlink to ../react-native/packages/react-native,
so the version below only has to satisfy the resolver. The native build reads the
react-native version out of the checkout: 1000.0.0, resolved from /tmp/maven-local
react-navigation and react-native-screens are deliberately absent. The RN screen in
this demo is a plain state stack over BackHandler, so the back behaviour under test is
React Native core's own and not FragmentManager's. A stack library would move the same
question into that library instead of answering it.
//setup: The react-native checkout is chosen by RN_REPO and defaults to ../react-native.
For the predictive-back PR (react-native#59292) checkout, export RN_REPO first:
yarn rn:publish                         # publishes that checkout as
yarn aar && yarn native:install         # fat AAR, then the app
Both shells need RN_REPO: yarn install uses it for the symlink and yarn start
uses it in metro.config.js. The native side cannot use the symlink at all
(see scripts/publish-rn.sh), so after any Java or C++ change in the checkout,
rerun yarn rn:publish before building. Without RN_REPO the fallback checkout
is used, which is a different branch.
//commands: The CLI's `bundle` command is registered by @react-native/community-cli-plugin through
its own react-native.config.js, and the CLI only reads that file for packages it finds
as direct dependencies of the project. Declared here for that reason, then symlinked
to the checkout by scripts/link.js like everything else from ../react-native.
